answer: One identity holds one county liquor license for one premises: the board caps the quota, vets owner and bar, and re-checks yearly on a live registry, so one license never covers two identities. An island county with twelve licenses charges $15,000 plus 180 days; the yarrow gin on the menu cannot hide a duplicate number. Cheapest cheat: a dormant rural license for $3,000, still needing a leased premises and a passed inspection; a bribed clerk costs $2,000 and risks a felony and revocation. As the quota fills, the price spirals up: one hundred fakes cost $1,500,000 and 18,000 days.
